# HR / Behavioral Phone Screen

[← Optiver](../README.md) · [Every Optiver question](../../optiver.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/hr-behavioral-screen)

`why-company`

---

## Requirements

- A roughly 20–30 minute conversation, generally held immediately after the OA, covering logistics, an in-depth discussion of one project, and motivation/fit.

## Examples

Commonly reported prompts include:

- Will you require sponsorship, or which visa do you hold; in what month do you expect to graduate?
- Introduce yourself; describe the project you are most proud of (start broadly, followed by deeper questions).
- Which elements of that project did you own rather than the team? How did you show initiative?
- Looking back, what would you change, and what prevented you from doing that originally?
- Describe an important decision you were responsible for making.
- Why Optiver? When and through what means did you first learn about Optiver?
- Which three qualities are most important in an engineer? Which are your strongest and weakest? What is your biggest weakness, and how are you working on it?
- If you received several offers, how would you choose among them (provide three reasons)? Are you also speaking with other companies?
- Preferred office: Chicago or Austin? What are your hobbies, or what was the last book you read and what did you take from it?

## Notes

- The follow-up that appears most consistently is the reflective probe, “what would you do differently / why were you unable to do it the first time?” — prepare an answer for your primary project.
- The recruiter generally explains the remaining interview stages at this point (usually two virtual rounds — one coding and one system-design round for SWE — followed, if successful, by an invitation to visit the Chicago office). Confirmation messages may sometimes contain private videos about the culture.

## Preparation

- Develop a concise project narrative that makes your individual ownership clear, along with the reflection on “what I would change and why.”
- Prepare concrete rather than generic responses for Why Optiver, your strengths and weaknesses, and the factors guiding an offer choice; be certain of your preferred office.
